common_chain: The merged account commonly carries 90%-100% close exposure in only two or three distinct symbols.
A synchronized loss often moves the account beyond 18% before the first close-confirmed drawdown event can act.
The existing close-to-next-open reduction path is causal but cannot undo an already-recorded close drawdown.
Warning state permits later buys in 28 failure scenarios, extending a minority of tails.
Therefore threshold-only retuning cannot be sufficient; an ex-ante account exposure/concentration budget is the required mechanism class.

preregistered_candidates.mechanism: At the first merged-account drawdown alert, cancel pending buys and queue a fixed 25% proportional account reduction for the next executable open; confirmation and emergency locks remain unchanged.
preregistered_candidates.causal_prediction: Improves continuation tails and removes warning-period risk additions, but cannot repair scenarios already beyond 18% at the first alert.

preregistered_candidates.mechanism: When the merged account holds at most three distinct symbols, enforce an 85% gross-exposure ceiling by scaling new buys and queuing proportional next-open reductions; the rule is symbol-, date-, scenario-, and seed-agnostic.
preregistered_candidates.causal_prediction: Creates headroom before synchronized losses and should address the dominant two-to-three-symbol failure cohort; prefix-05 wealth retention is the decisive cost check.

redesign_budget.condition: Use only if C1 and C2 provide causal evidence yet neither satisfies both the 18% safety boundary and return protections.
